title: How Long Is Phantom Blade Zero? 20-25 Hours Main, 50-70 to Platinum
description: Phantom Blade Zero playtime, measured: 20-25 hours for the main story, 30-40 with side content, 40-45 for a full clear, 50-70 for the platinum - and why reviewers reported 50 hours when the director said 20 to 30.
keyword: how long is phantom blade zero, phantom blade zero length, phantom blade zero how long to beat, phantom blade zero playtime, phantom blade zero hours

facts.label: Reviewer runs
facts.value: 50 hours (IGN) and 55 hours (Combo Infinito) at review

facts.label: Replay
facts.value: 66 Days mode unlocks after any completion; New Game Plus carries gear over

sections.title: The Answer
sections.content:
20 to 25 hours if you chase the story and nothing else. 30 to 40 hours if you take the side content, which is the way the game is meant to be played and the range the guides themselves cannot agree on. 40 to 45 hours to clear everything, stretching to 50-55 if you are thorough, and 50 to 70 if you are going for the platinum.

This page used to say the figure was unconfirmed. It was, in September. It is not now, and the pre-release framing has been replaced rather than annotated.

The spread is not noise. Two different things are being measured: the guides' 20-25 hours is a main-path run that skips optional bosses and Tales, while the reviewers' 50 hours is a first playthrough that engaged with the side content because the game pushes you toward it.

sections.title: Why Reviewers Said 50 Hours and the Director Said 20 to 30
sections.content:
The director's 20-30 hour figure is a story estimate, and 20-25 is what it turns into once you actually route it. The review runs are longer for three compounding reasons:

  • Boss gates. The combat is deflect-and-punish, so a fight that costs one player fifteen minutes costs another an hour. Several bosses in the roster are hard walls on a first attempt.
  • Optional content is not optional in practice. Weapons, accessories and Sha-Chi Amber Shards come from side areas. Skip them and the back half gets harder, which lengthens the back half.
  • The Tales are story. Purple Tales feed the endings, so anyone reviewing the narrative had to do them.

IGN's reviewer wrote that combat 'never came even close to feeling old across 50 hours', which is the useful data point: the extra 25 hours were not padding being endured.

sections.title: What Actually Drives Your Number
sections.content:
Four levers, in order of impact:

Difficulty. Four modes - Wayfarer, Pathbreaker, Hellwalker and 66 Days. Wayfarer exists specifically for players who want the story and the combat without the wall; Hellwalker makes enemies adaptive. There is no difficulty trophy, so Wayfarer costs you nothing but pride.

Whether you do the Acolytes and Lóng Pillars. That is four boss fights and five duels against the Gold-Masked One, and the later pillars are fought at your current power level, so leaving them late makes them expensive.

Collectibles. Seven tracked categories: bells, challenge locations, weapons and Phantom Edges, accessories and medicines, Sha-Chi Amber Shards, Blackstone Shards, and Memory Flowers. Accessories alone are 30 for the Collector's Note trophy.

Tempering. Upgrade and Temper trophies want one weapon at level 30 and ten weapons plus ten Phantom Edges Tempered. Tempering is refundable, so this is time rather than resources.

sections.title: Post-Game and Replay
sections.content:
Free roam opens after the credits: bells work, regions stay open, and cleanup is possible. What does not come back is any Tale that expired at the Mount Soulrend climb.

66 Days unlocks after any completion - 66 lives for a whole run, save deleted on the 66th death. Dying out of it is the only way to see the secret ending, so a completionist's hour count includes a deliberate failure somewhere.

New Game Plus carries skills, weapons and Phantom Edges over, which is the recovery path if something missable slipped past you. It is also why the platinum is rated 7/10 rather than higher - nothing is permanently lost, only delayed.

Chapter order is on the walkthrough; the trophy requirements are on the trophy guide.
